items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ted Pankin, who writes for Down Beat and is a very good writer, is working on it as we speak... he’s been working on it... he does the research

ctx.x: When can we expect a book?

Well, Ted Pankin, who writes for Down Beat and is a very good writer, is working on it as we speak. I mean, I took it as far as I could and I realized that I don’t know anything about the book business. I mean, the record business is hard enough, but the book business is really--, getting it published and all that. And then I realized that I’m an amateur writer. I mean, I can tell a story, but--. So he’s been working on it, just making it ea…not changing he’s not changing my words he’s just making it more…

it’s my life and the stories and uh. You know, because as I say, I was perched historically at a very important time, you know, after the Second World War when the cultural explosion, and you know, getting to know Bird and Dizzy and you know. I played with everybody, so it’s not so that I’m important, but it’s important with all the people I know and learned from. So, I wanted to share that and make sure it was documented. So, I mean, I figure after, when I’m gone I know it’ll be published, because my records…
